page: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-64 is a dedicated x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine profile designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 992.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.5 GB per virtual CPU. It contains no attached GPU hardware accelerators.

Storage configuration relies completely on remote persistent block volumes, as the m4-hypermem-64 does not provision local NVMe SSD storage. Network attachment does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured cloud NAT or provisioned static IPs for external networking. Architectural tradeoffs focus strictly on massive centralized RAM rather than local high-throughput ephemeral disk structures.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the machine consolidates substantial memory requirements into a single system image, avoiding distributed coordination overhead for large in-memory footprints. Workloads aligned with this resource profile include large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, enterprise relational database management systems, heavy in-memory analytics, and extensive caching tiers.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-64 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for substantial memory footprints. Featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 992.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an expansive 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU without hardware GPU acceleration. The configuration includes zero local storage, meaning disk operations require network-attached persistent storage volumes. Network routing relies on private address space by default, with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned. By providing a high memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance maximizes operational density for workloads constrained by RAM rather than raw compute or local I/O throughput. The m4-hypermem-64 is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, SAP HANA installations, and high-capacity data analytics engines requiring vast memory capacity under a single compute node.
